units.text: Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.

I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.
I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.
Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.
Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.
No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.

Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.
Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.
I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.
I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.
All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.

Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.
The cost of rebuilding and renewing the works of the holy places shall be given from the king’s account.
The cost of rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls and fortifying it all around shall be given from the king’s account, and likewise for rebuilding walls in Judea.”
When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they neither believed nor accepted them, because they remembered the great evil he had committed in Israel and how severely he had oppressed them.
They favoured Alexander, because he had been the first to speak peaceful words to them, and they remained his allies all his days.
He took the sons of the leaders of the country as hostages and placed them under guard in the citadel at Jerusalem.
In the second month of the one hundred and fifty-third year, Alcimus ordered the wall of the inner court of the holy places to be demolished. He began tearing down the works of the prophets.
At that time Alcimus was struck, and his work was obstructed. His mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, unable to speak another word or give orders concerning his household.
Alcimus died at that time in great torment.
Behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the Lord’s word, while Jeroboam stood at the altar to offer sacrifice.

He called to the altar by the Lord’s word: “Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. He will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.”
He gave a portent that day, saying, “This is the word the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will split, and the fat upon it will pour out.”

When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.

King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Entreat the favor of the Lord your God, and let my hand be restored to me.” The man of God entreated the Lord’s favor, and he restored the king’s hand to him, so it became as it had been before.
After Elihu ceased speaking, the Lord spoke to Job through a whirlwind and clouds:
“Who is this who hides counsel from Me, holding words within his heart, and thinks he hides them from Me?
Gird your waist like a man; I will question you, and you must answer Me.
But in the first year of Cyrus the king, King Cyrus issued a decision for this house of God to be built.

And the gold and silver vessels of God’s house that Nabouchodonosor took from the house in Jerusalem and carried to the king’s sanctuary—King Cyrus took them from the king’s sanctuary and gave them to Sasabasar, the treasury keeper in charge of the treasury,
and said to him, ‘Take all the vessels, go and place them in the house in Jerusalem, in their own place.’
Then that Sasabasar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now it has been built, but it has not been completed.’

Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the treasury house of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that King Cyrus issued a decision to build that house of God in Jerusalem. When the king has learned about this, let him send word to us.”
Judas, also called Maccabeus, and those with him slipped secretly into the villages, called their kinsmen to join them, and gathered those who had remained in Judaism, assembling about six thousand.
They called upon the Lord to look upon the people trampled by everyone, and to have pity on the temple profaned by impious men,
to have mercy also on the city being destroyed and about to be levelled, and to listen to the blood crying out to Him,
to remember the unlawful destruction of innocent infants and the blasphemies committed against His name, and to show His hatred of wickedness.
Once Maccabeus had formed his company, he became irresistible to the nations, the Lord’s anger having turned to mercy.
